subject: pathology
title: Megaloblastic and macrocytic anaemias

steps.tx: **Macrocytic anaemia** develops when red cells become large because DNA synthesis is impaired in the marrow. The commonest causes are **vitamin B12 deficiency** and folate deficiency, which delay nuclear division while cytoplasm continues to grow. Blood therefore shows macroovalocytes and **hypersegmented neutrophils**, while marrow shows large megaloblastic precursors. Macrocytosis from alcohol, liver disease or hypothyroidism lacks hypersegmentation and therefore points away from megaloblastic change.
steps.say: Macrocytic anaemia is a condition where large red cells appear because DNA synthesis is impaired in the marrow. Vitamin B12 deficiency and folate deficiency cause this problem because nuclei divide slowly while cytoplasm keeps growing. The blood film shows macroovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils, which help clinicians separate megaloblastic change from alcohol related macrocytosis.

steps.tx: **Vitamin B12** absorption requires intrinsic factor from the stomach and a healthy terminal ileum for uptake. Pernicious anaemia and ileal disease or resection therefore cause deficiency because absorption fails at these sites. **Folate** is absorbed in the jejunum and body stores become depleted within months of poor intake. Liver stores of vitamin B12 last for years, so the timing of symptoms after surgery helps locate the cause.
steps.say: Vitamin B12 absorption is a process that requires intrinsic factor and a healthy terminal ileum for successful uptake. Folate stores are depleted within months because the body keeps only a small reserve in tissues. This timing difference helps clinicians date the deficiency after gastric surgery or major dietary change.

steps.tx: Only vitamin B12 deficiency injures the nervous system, and it does so through **subacute combined degeneration** of the spinal cord. The dorsal and lateral columns are damaged, so vibration sense and proprioception fail early in the illness. Patients develop brisk reflexes and extensor plantar responses because corticospinal tracts are also involved in the lesion. **Glossitis** and anaemia often accompany the cord signs, and delayed treatment leaves permanent neurological damage.
steps.say: Only vitamin B12 deficiency damages the spinal cord because it causes subacute combined degeneration of dorsal and lateral columns. Vibration sense and proprioception fail early because the dorsal columns carry these signals to the brain. Treatment is urgent because delayed replacement allows permanent cord damage even when blood counts recover.

steps.tx: This spinal MRI shows bright signal in the dorsal columns forming an **inverted V sign** on axial imaging. That pattern reflects **subacute combined degeneration** caused by vitamin B12 deficiency in the spinal cord. Dorsal column damage explains why vibration sense and proprioception fail before severe weakness develops in patients. Recognising this image helps candidates link macrocytic anaemia with gait disturbance and extensor plantar responses in exam stems.
steps.say: This MRI image is showing dorsal column hyperintensity because vitamin B12 deficiency damages the posterior spinal cord columns. The inverted V sign is important because it visually confirms subacute combined degeneration in the cord. Examiners favour this image because it helps clinicians connect anaemia with vibration loss and gait disturbance.

steps.tx: **Pernicious anaemia** is an autoimmune disease where parietal cells in the stomach are destroyed by immune attack. Loss of parietal cells causes achlorhydria and failure of intrinsic factor production in the stomach. Antibodies against **intrinsic factor** are specific for the diagnosis, while parietal cell antibodies are sensitive but less specific. The condition is associated with other autoimmune diseases and carries an increased risk of gastric cancer.
steps.say: Pernicious anaemia is an autoimmune condition where parietal cells are destroyed and intrinsic factor production fails completely. Intrinsic factor antibody testing is specific because this antibody rarely appears in other gastric diseases. Associated autoimmune disease and gastric cancer risk are features that examiners frequently test in clinical stems.

steps.tx: Folate deficiency around conception causes **neural tube defects** because the neural tube closes very early in pregnancy. Periconception folate supplementation therefore prevents these defects rather than treating them after closure has failed. Methotrexate and other antifolate drugs reproduce megaloblastic change because they block folate dependent DNA synthesis. **Folate alone** must never be given before vitamin B12 is checked, because correcting blood counts can mask progressing cord injury.
steps.say: Folate deficiency around conception causes neural tube defects because the neural tube closes before most pregnancies are recognised. Folate alone is dangerous before vitamin B12 status is checked because blood counts improve while cord injury progresses. This masking effect is the reason clinicians measure both vitamins before starting treatment.
